residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a bona fide resident of Nebraska for at least one year, or must have been stationed in Nebraska as a member of the military for one year, immediately preceding the filing of the complaint. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §42-349)

waitingPeriod.description: No decree may be entered until at least 60 days after the filing or service of the complaint, whichever is later. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §42-372)

groundsForDissolution.notes: Nebraska is a no-fault only state. The sole ground for dissolution is that the marriage is irretrievably broken. (Neb. Rev. Stat. §42-361)

propertyDivision.description: Nebraska courts divide marital property equitably (not necessarily equally). The court considers contributions of each spouse, the duration of the marriage, the circumstances of the parties, interruptions to careers or education, and the ability of a supported spouse to engage in gainful employment without interfering with the interests of a minor child.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property owned before the marriage or acquired by gift or inheritance may be considered separate, but the court has broad discretion to include all property in the division.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirement — 1 year state residency or 1 year military stationing
Grounds for dissolution — marriage is irretrievably broken (no-fault only)
60-day waiting period from filing or service
Property division and alimony — equitable distribution
Nebraska Child Support Guidelines — income shares model

filingFees.notes: Nebraska filing fee for a complaint for dissolution of marriage is $164 as of July 1, 2025 (per the Nebraska Judicial Branch fee schedule). Some counties may charge slightly different amounts. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Financial Affidavit
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Dissolution of Marriage
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on respondent via sheriff or process server

service.name: Voluntary Appearance
service.description: Respondent waives formal service and enters appearance
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Required parenting plan detailing custody and parenting time arrangements

withChildren.name: Child Support Calculation Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Nebraska Child Support Guidelines (Neb. Rev. Stat. §42-364.16)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

inState.description: Respondent must file an answer within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Nebraska must file an answer within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Nebraska uses an income shares model. Both parents' monthly net incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Nebraska Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined monthly net income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate. Parenting time credits may apply.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Nebraska courts may award alimony based on the circumstances of the parties, the duration of the marriage, the contributions of each spouse to the marriage, the ability of the supported spouse to engage in gainful employment, and the ability of the other spouse to pay.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: There is no formula. The court considers the needs of the requesting spouse and the paying spouse's ability to pay, along with the factors in Neb. Rev. Stat. §42-365.

court.name: District Court
court.description: Dissolution of marriage is filed in the District Court of the county where either party resides.
